title: 162 UAP files on war.gov: what lies behind the first batch
excerpt: 162 UAP files published by the US Department of War on war.gov/ufo on May 8, 2026. What they actually contain and how to analyze them rigorously and in 3D.
content:
On May 8, 2026, the United States Department of War opened war.gov/ufo with 162 files on unidentified anomalous phenomena. The topic comes from a 2026 Milenio 3 special (Cadena SER). At foro3d.com we will follow the images with a cool head and 3D at the forefront.

What was said versus what is known today 🔍

The figure of 162 files was repeated widely in the media, but the Pentagon itself warned that the documents had been reviewed for security, not analyzed to resolve each anomaly, and that more batches would be released. That does not amount to proof of anything extraordinary: previous official reports from the AARO office have found no evidence of extraterrestrial technology, and some videos admit ordinary explanations, such as sensor glints, birds or flares.

The file that is always about to be opened 📂

The PURSUE initiative, ordered by Donald Trump in February, promises more batches, and the enthusiast's patience is put to the test. Meanwhile, the old FBI reports from the late forties and material from NASA's Apollo missions continue to feed the legend of the folder that is never quite opened. What do you expect to find in the next files? Tell us.
